$comment: ADG SMB collector target configuration. Copy to adg-smb-targets.json and edit.
This file contains no credentials and must never contain any: the collector runs as
the identity of its own process, so that there is no password to store. Every value
$comment_servers: Host names or FQDNs, never UNC paths. There is no domain-wide sweep: ADG scans what you list and nothing else, so that a run's declared scope always means something exact.
$comment_protocol: Wsman (WinRM, TCP 5985/5986) or Dcom (RPC 135 plus the dynamic range). Wsman is usually the easier of the two to allow through a firewall.
$comment_timeouts: Bounds on how long one unreachable server may cost. The delay grows with each attempt, so retryCount 2 with retryDelaySeconds 2 spends at most about six seconds past the timeouts before giving up on a dead host.
$comment_batchSize: Observations per batch, at most 1000. Smaller batches make a retry cheaper.
$comment_aclMethod: Auto reads the share security descriptor (SIDs and raw access masks) and falls back to the permission levels when it cannot. Pin it to Descriptor or Access in a mixed estate: the two forms are legitimately different readings of one ACL, and alternating between them churns the history for no reason.
$comment_patterns: Wildcard patterns matched against the share name, case-insensitively. An exclude always beats an include. When includeShares is non-empty, only matching shares are recorded.
$comment_defaults: Administrative shares (C$, ADMIN$, IPC$) are excluded because their ACL is a Windows constant rather than an organizational decision. Ordinary hidden shares (Data$) are excluded by default too, but they ARE an organizational decision - turn includeHiddenShares on if your estate uses them to publish real data.
$comment_recordExcludedShares: Record that an excluded share exists without reading its ACL. Leave it on: it is what lets a run honestly claim to have enumerated every share on the server, which is in turn what lets ADG notice that a share was deleted. Turning it off hides excluded shares completely, and deletions on that server stop being detectable.
